assets: comment bodies of four independent communities
the mapping between a person and their comments on one site
trust_boundaries: site adapter to shared API (scope asserted by host or credential)
API to database (scope carried on every statement)
platform to tenant operators (RBAC, default deny)

threats.threat: cross-tenant read by guessing or leaking an id
threats.control: tenant pair in every primary key, composite foreign keys, scope re-asserted on every row read, 404 rather than 403

threats.threat: a client naming its own tenant
stored XSS through a comment body
threats.control: escape everything, then rebuild only allowlisted constructs

threats.threat: cross-site request forgery on a write
threats.control: CSRF token required on unsafe methods under cookie auth

threats.threat: IDOR on edit, delete, react or report
threats.control: ownership checked separately from the grant; scope first
every statement is parameterised; no string interpolation of values
four independent rate buckets, exact and near duplicate detection, deterministic risk scoring, fail closed

threats.threat: report brigading used to hide a comment
threats.control: reporters per distinct network compared before queueing
public ids derived under per-tenant keys; no shared identifier

threats.threat: privilege escalation by a tenant operator
threats.control: default deny, platform-only permissions, no self-elevation, four-eyes on rollout, short-lived scoped service tokens
SSR renders published states only and is gated on publication

threats.threat: comment text leaking into logs, metrics or audit
threats.control: audit stores a shape; metric labels are an allowlist

threats.threat: a comments outage breaking the host page
threats.control: every widget entry point guarded; API failure degrades to a notice
the platform never fetches a URL from a comment; links are rendered as text with an http(s) scheme check

accepted_residual.item: a small layout shift in user_initiated mode
accepted_residual.why: thread height is unknowable before the fetch
accepted_residual.mitigation: reserved height; ssr_* modes eliminate it

accepted_residual.item: network HMAC is reversible by brute force within an epoch
accepted_residual.why: the address space is small; this is inherent to any IP-derived value
accepted_residual.mitigation: daily rotation, 7-day retention, per-tenant key, never logged
